<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. IIII.|ACCORDING TO S. IOHN.|227}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=4|verse=39}}† And of that citie many beleeued in him of the Samaritans, for the vvord of the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ This woman mystically being the Church, it is here signified, that they which at the first beleeue because the Church teacheth so, afterward be much confirmed, finding it in the Scripture also, and by other instructions.}}∷ vvoman giuing testimonie, that he told me al things vvhatsoeuer I haue done. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=40}}† Therfore vvhen the Samaritans vvere come to him, they desired him that he vvould tarie there. And he taried there tvvo daies. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=41}}† And many moe beleeued for his ovvne vvord. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=42}}† And they said to the vvoman, That novv not for thy saying doe vve beleeue: for our selues haue heard, and doe knovv that this is the Sauiour of the vvorld in deede.⊣ {{verse|chapter=4|verse=43}}† And after the tvvo daies he departed thence: and vvent into Galilee. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=44}}† For {{sc|Iesvs}} him self gaue testimonie that a Prophet hath not honour in his ovvne countrie. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=45}}† Therfore {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 4, 12. Mr. 1, 14. Luc. 4, 14.''}}* vvhen he vvas come into Galilee, the Galilaeans receiued him, vvhereas they had seen al things that he had done at Hierusalem in the festiual day: for them selues also came to the festiual day.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=46}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 2, 9.''}}* He came againe therfore into Cana of Galilee, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 20 Sunday after Pentecost.}}VVhere he made vvater vvine. And there vvas a certaine lord vvhose sonne was sicke at Capharnáum. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=47}}† He hauing heard that {{sc|Iesvs}} came from Ievvrie into Galilee, vvent to him, and desired him that he vvould come dovvne & heale his sonne. for he began to die. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=48}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} therfore said to him, Vnlesse you see signes and vvonders, you beleeue not. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=49}}† The lord saith to him, Lord, come dovvne before that my sonne die. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=50}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, Goe, thy sonne liueth. The man beleeued the vvord that {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, and vvent. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=51}}† And as he vvas novv going dovvne, his seruants mette him: and they brought vvord, saying, That his sonne liued. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=52}}† He asked therfore of them the houre, vvherein he vvas amended. And they said to him, That yesterday at the seuenth houre the feuer left him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=53}}† The father therfore knevv that it vvas in the same houre vvherein {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Thy sonne liueth. and him self beleeued and his vvhole house.⊣ {{verse|chapter=4|verse=54}}† This againe the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 2, 11.''}}* second signe did {{sc|Iesvs}}, vvhen he vvas come from Ievvrie into Galilee.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. IIII.}}}}

''20. Our Fathers adored.'') By adoration is meant doing of sacrifice. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Schismatical temple contendeth against the true Temple.}}for other offices of Religion might be done in any place. The Samaritanes to defend their adoring in Garizim, pretended their worshiping there to be more ancient then the Iewes in Hierusalem, referring it to<noinclude>{{rh||Ff ij|Iacob:}}</noinclude>
